system_description.narrative_title: Iran-linked regional escalation reshaping security and energy markets
system_description.narrative_summary: A surge in hostilities and threats tied to Iran and its proxies (Houthis, Hezbollah, allied actors) is driving military posturing, evacuations and heightened embassy security, while prompting urgent diplomacy to prevent wider war. The crisis is already distorting global energy markets, maritime operations and critical infrastructure risk assessments, producing cascading economic and security effects beyond the Middle East.
system_description.scope: Interactions among Iran, its regional proxies, Gulf states, the United States and allied partners; military strikes, missile/drone attacks, security alerts and evacuations; diplomatic mediation efforts; impacts on oil and gas markets, shipping, undersea infrastructure and regional economic stability.
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil & gas markets and strategic petroleum reserves
US domestic politics and electoral timing (midterms)
Maritime commerce and undersea communications infrastructure
Gulf intra-state security arrangements and regional diplomacy
evidence_headlines: American embassies tighten security as Iran threat warnings intensify ahead of U.S. midterm elections
Oil hits $117 for first time since April on fears of flare-up in Iran hostilities
Intelligence memo warns Iran is plotting to kill Americans in Middle East
Houthis say they attacked Saudi oil pumping stations, Riyadh airport as fighting intensifies
Qatari mediators in Tehran for U.S.-coordinated effort to ease tensions
Iran has detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if war resumes, officials say

variables.name: Regional conflict intensity
variables.description: The aggregated severity and tempo of hostile military interactions across the region, measured continuously by incident severity, casualty estimates and operational scope.

variables.name: Proxy attack rate
variables.description: The rate at which non-state aligned armed actors conduct offensive operations (raids, strikes, sabotage) per unit time.

variables.name: Cross-border strike frequency
variables.description: The frequency of missile, drone and other long-range strikes that traverse international boundaries per unit time.

variables.name: Military deployment and readiness level
variables.description: The aggregate posture and mobilization level of armed forces in the theater, including deployment density and alert status.

variables.name: Diplomatic mediation activity
variables.description: The intensity and frequency of formal and informal mediation efforts, negotiations and shuttle diplomacy taking place per unit time.

variables.name: De‑escalation signal strength
variables.description: The perceived strength and credibility of signals and actions indicating reductions in hostilities or commitments to restraint.

variables.name: Oil price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price per barrel for benchmark crude as a continuous market state.

variables.name: Oil price volatility
variables.description: The short- and medium-term variability of oil prices, measured by realized or implied volatility over a rolling horizon.

variables.name: Energy supply disruption risk premium
variables.description: The component of energy prices attributable to market perceptions of disruption risk to supply chains and infrastructure.

variables.name: Seaborne transport disruption rate
variables.description: The rate at which maritime cargo movements (especially energy shipments) are delayed, rerouted, interdicted or denied access per unit time.

variables.name: Undersea infrastructure vulnerability
variables.description: The level of exposure and fragility of subsea cables, pipelines and related seabed assets to physical attack or accidental damage.

variables.name: Shipping insurance premium level
variables.description: The prevailing additional insurance costs (war, hull, route risk) charged for maritime shipments as a continuous market measure.

variables.name: Strategic reserve release rate
variables.description: The volumetric rate at which strategic petroleum or fuel reserves are released into markets or logistics networks per unit time.

variables.name: Alternative energy routing flow
variables.description: The volume of energy (oil, refined products, gas) reallocated through non-standard routes, storage or suppliers per unit time.

variables.name: Regional economic spillover intensity
variables.description: The magnitude and speed at which security shocks transmit to regional economic indicators (trade, markets, investment) as a continuous state.

catalysts.title: Intensified Tehran mediation effort
catalysts.description: Qatar- and Mecca-pact-led talks in Tehran ramp up coordinated diplomacy to prevent fresh escalation.
catalysts.rationale: Qatari mediators in Tehran; Mecca-pact officials to meet Iranian officials; Saudi defence pact push for peace in Tehran.

catalysts.title: Renewed Houthi attack campaign
catalysts.description: Houthis continue and intensify strikes on Saudi infrastructure, airports and shipping hubs, sustaining cross-border operations.
catalysts.rationale: Houthis say they attacked Saudi oil pumping stations, Riyadh airport; Houthis launch more attacks; warnings against using Riyadh airport.

catalysts.title: U.S. decision on military strikes
catalysts.description: U.S. leadership faces a near-term decision whether to conduct further military operations against Iranian-linked targets.
catalysts.rationale: Trump envoy/Trump say soon to decide; Trump says US may do another military operation; USS George Washington rearming.

catalysts.title: Evacuations and allied redeployments
catalysts.description: U.S. and partners continue evacuations of personnel and rearm frontline assets, raising regional force posture and alerts.
catalysts.rationale: U.S. evacuates Mideast outposts; American embassies tighten security; USS George Washington rearming.

catalysts.title: Strategic releases and Singapore storage moves
catalysts.description: Emergency U.S. releases and accelerated Saudi oil storage in Singapore increase available market supply and strategic buffering.
catalysts.rationale: US authorizes emergency release of up to 400,000 barrels; Saudi oil to be stored in Singapore caverns.

catalysts.title: Asian supply diplomacy and export adjustments
catalysts.description: Indonesia, Singapore, Petronas and regional actors negotiate supply routes, storage and conditional approvals to shore up regional fuel availability.
catalysts.rationale: Indonesia energy minister to visit China, India; Indonesia cuts pipeline gas exports; Petronas regional power corridor approval.

catalysts.title: Threats to Gulf undersea infrastructure
catalysts.description: Publicized Iranian plans to target undersea cables raise the risk profile, prompting potential attacks or protective deployments.
catalysts.rationale: Officials say Iran has detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables, raising infrastructure risk and response.
